why: Angso is built with its own builder (angsobuild/reconcile.mjs from the reviewed orthophoto records), and is not traced from decisions. This configuration lets pipeline v2's looks read it: the ring sheets, the deck check and the photo windows read the published outlines from playing-surfaces.geojson, which packages/course-geo/mapping/export-model-surfaces.mjs writes from the model's migration record. The tracer is never run on it.

compare.why: The other photo years over the same box (angsobuild/run-ortho-intake.mjs): pass one as --compare.

terrain.why: Read again on 2026-11-26 with build-ground-rings.mjs --ground angso --only 0. Lantmateriet republished item 660_60 on 2026-09-14, so its checksum is not the 2026-09-04 one in ground-rings.json; against the published terrain it differs by 2 mm on average and 6 cm at its worst sample (98 of 16.9 million samples outside the quantum).

sand.measured: Angso's raked sand is tan, not white: on the 2025-04-24 photo the 33 reviewed bunkers, read 0.6 m in from their edge, have brightness 95-152 (median 123), NDVI -0.16 to -0.04 (median -0.13) and warmth 6-25 (median 14), against the turf 3-8 m round them at brightness 74-114, NDVI +0.09 to +0.36 and warmth -7 to 16 (5th to 95th percentile; measured 2026-11-27).
sand.bands: Core is the inner half of the measured sand (brightness 108-190, NDVI under -0.11, warmth 8-28), so that the gravel paths (grey, warmth under 8), red roofs (warmth over 28) and bare spring soil (NDVI near 0) the looser bands found do not read as sand; a patch grows over the looser band.
